newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlers rebuild demolished structure.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlers rebuild demolished structure.

text.p: Jewish settlers on Wednesday rebuilt a shack demolished a day earlier by Israeli police at a West Bank settlement, settlers said.
"We took a hammer and nails and said, okay, we have to start rebuilding what was destroyed and that is what we did," a settler, identified as Yossi, said to Israel Army radio.
Police forcibly removed dozens of settlers from a shack outside the Yitzhar settlement on Tuesday and destroyed it along with two other wooden structures they said were built illegally.
Several children, who had been in the shack, were lightly injured by shards of glass and 18 settlers were arrested.
Members of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition threatened to bolt over the incident.

"If we find the government's policy is not what it says about building settlements it will be very hard for us to stay in the government," said Minister Yitzhak Levy of the National Religious Party, which has nine of the 66 seats the 120-member parliament.

Jewish settler leader Pinchas Walerstein accused the government of destroying the structures as a gesture towards the Palestinians ahead of Tuesday night's meeting between Israeli President Ezer Weizman and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
"What happened yesterday was aimed at showing Arafat 'look how we treat settlers', ahead of the meeting with Weizman. It was a clear cynical act," Walerstein told Israel radio.

The Weizman-Arafat talks came ahead of U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross's return to the region on Wednesday to try to revive Israeli-Palestinian peace talks. Ross is scheduled to meet Netanyahu on Wednesday night.

Israel captured the West Bank and the Gaza Strip in the 1967 Middle East war. More than 130,000 Israelis have since settled amid some two million Palestinians in the occupied areas, not counting Arab East Jersualem.

Under a framework 1993 peace deal Israel has handed much of the Gaza Strip and some of the West Bank to Palestinian rule. Final peace talks have yet to resume under Netanyahu who took office last June.
